title: Parameters and Database
summary: Parameter profiles store reusable values, metadata, aliases and context JSON. Open Parameter Store at /parameter-editor to manage them, then reference a key with @name in Chat. By default.

headings.title: Review a successful binding for future tasks
Correct a tool call and remember its mapping

html:
Parameters and Database

Parameter profiles store reusable values, metadata, aliases and context JSON. Open Parameter Store at /parameter-editor to manage them, then reference a key with @name in Chat. By default, ordinary parameters supply exact saved inputs to tools while the Agent sees their structure and guidance. Recognized typed credential profiles retain their existing private credential handling.

database.discover_schema and database.execute use the existing PostgreSQL implementation. The model first discovers the tools, selects the scoped profile and sends concrete SQL. The execution layer validates SQL and mutation authorization. Account/profile resolution remains separate from model tool selection.

Context JSON and parameter metadata are useful facts for the model. They do not select a tool before the model sees the user's request. Ordinary requests such as “query the research database” enter the agent loop.

Open Parameter Store from Directory. Search by key or filter by tag, select a profile, or use New to create one. Enter a key, choose JSON or FREE FORM above the Value text field, add optional context or agent guidance, and save. JSON requires a non-empty object. Free form accepts plain text without JSON validation and preserves spacing and line breaks. Saved free-form values reopen in text mode. Direct links such as /parameter-editor?key=canonical_v1 select a profile. Save updates the value, description, aliases, tags, and context fields. Existing values stay hidden in the editor until you choose Reveal & edit value; saving metadata while hidden preserves the stored value.

Use context summary and prompt guidance for compact domain guidance, clarification guidance for ambiguity handling, and concepts, metrics, and relationships for structured domain facts. Advanced context JSON preserves additional non-secret metadata. Invalid JSON blocks saving in JSON mode and in structured context fields. Unsaved edits are protected when navigating between profiles, and Ctrl/Cmd+S saves.

Default output directories

These entries are added automatically when the Parameter Store opens, including existing installations. Users do not need to create them. Search for their names or environment variables in the composer's Parameter Store menu.

Reference Meaning Gateway environment variable
@run_temp_directory Collected temporary files shared across commands in one run, such as commit messages and helper scripts OF_RUN_TEMP_DIR
@artifact_output_directory Final deliverables to display or download, such as plots and reports OF_RUN_ARTIFACT_DIR
@activity_temp_directory Collected temporary files for the current execution activity; may change between tool calls TMPDIR on Linux/macOS, TEMP/TMP on Windows

For example: Plot x+y=1, save the PNG in @artifact_output_directory, and show me the image.

These entries store environment-variable references and usage guidance, not fixed filesystem paths. Shell/Python reads the variable during execution on the selected Gateway. Accepting or queuing a task does not freeze a previous run's directory. For example, Python uses Path(os.environ["OF_RUN_ARTIFACT_DIR"]) / "plot.png". The Gateway supplies these variables; users do not need to set TEMPDIR or create an arbitrary /tmp directory. Missing entries are restored the next time the store opens; existing values and user edits are preserved.

Reference only the directories the task needs. In the checked-out implementation, selecting all three default entries together in bound mode exceeds the default 4,000-character manifest limit. The task is held before inference; use fewer references or adjust the configured limit described below.

Free-form text is stored in the free_form_text field of the parameter value, so existing @name references and parameter bindings can use it.

JSON templates and typed profiles

The selector beside New offers Blank, Server, Proxmox Server, Credential, Hugging Face Token, Git Repository, Gmail OAuth App, Gmail Account, Google Workspace OAuth App, Google Workspace Account, and HTTP Connection with Basic, Bearer, API Key, Session Login and OAuth2 starters. Choose a template and click New to prefill an unsaved draft (HTTP uses structured fields; other templates use Value JSON); Format JSON, Save, masking and Reveal & edit value retain their existing roles. Selecting a template does not save a record, open a connection or enable a skill.

Recognized server_connection, credential, huggingface_token, git_repository, gmail_oauth_app, gmail_account, google_oauth_app and google_account profiles use profile_version: 1. Save validates required fields, types and unknown fields. Server profiles require HTTPS, a hostname/IP without a URL path, an integer port from 1 to 65535 and a Boolean verify_tls. Proxmox accounts include their realm, such as root@pam. Credentials belong in the password/token fields, not an embedded Git URL. Validation errors identify the field and rule without echoing private values. Untyped arbitrary JSON retains its previous behavior.

See Using Proxmox VE for the optional, disabled-by-default skill and Proxmox authentication for secure input, session renewal and cleanup.

Hugging Face tokens

Choose Hugging Face Token beside New, click New, and enter a key such as hf. Replace the empty token in Value JSON with your access token from Hugging Face token settings, then Save. A read token or fine-grained token with access to the intended repository supports downloads; see Hugging Face access tokens. The profile contains only profile_type: "huggingface_token", profile_version: 1, and a nonempty string token. Saving validates these fields without contacting Hugging Face or starting a download.

Reference the saved entry with @hf, for example: Use @hf to download the selected GGUF file into /mnt/models. Choose the repository, exact files, and destination for each task. Token visibility follows the existing configurable Parameters redaction policy, and Reveal & edit value lets you replace the saved token.

For commands running with the Parameter Store shell environment export, the key hf exports its token as OF_PARAM_HF_TOKEN. Map it to Hugging Face's HF_TOKEN for the download command:

HF_TOKEN="${OF_PARAM_HF_TOKEN:?Parameter Store token has not been exported}" \
  hf download example/model weights.gguf --local-dir /mnt/models

Replace example/model and weights.gguf with the requested repository and file. An @hf reference supplies the saved parameter to the Agent; it does not set environment variables in an existing terminal.

Saved HTTP connections

Choose HTTP Connection (or an authentication starter) beside New and configure the saved profile under a key such as production_api. The current validator requires profile_version: 3 with literal provider fields, for example auth.token for Bearer authentication. Templates prefill configuration; selecting one does not authenticate or contact the endpoint. Version 1/2 profiles, private credential maps and slot references are unsupported and must be recreated.

Save credentials as part of the profile. The former separate credentials endpoint is retired. Saving replaces the submitted portable configuration, so omitted credential fields are not restored from the old record. The structured editor preserves untouched sections; when a profile is redacted, use Reveal & edit value to edit its actual raw configuration. Reveal is explicit and audited. PARAMETERS controls ordinary inspection copies; it does not change stored execution values.

Test connection explicitly runs the configured bounded GET/HEAD/OPTIONS request from the selected or default Gateway. Opening a profile does not test it. Disconnect Session clears runtime authentication while retaining saved values; deleting the Parameter removes the record and invalidates sessions. Metadata, rename and @ reference controls remain part of Parameter Store.

For example: Use @production_api and GET /health. Use the exact saved key with http.request(profile_key="production_api", method="GET", url="/health"). Ordinary accepted references retain their captured literal values, while protected OAuth/auth_ref profiles retain their existing private authority rules. HTTP tools apply their own current-record, revision and scoped-session checks.

There is no separate HTTP editor in Settings. One-off http.connect handles remain scoped to the current run, Gateway and origin and do not create Parameters. The HTTP / REST guide is the authoritative reference for providers, literal fields, editor behavior, session recovery and transport limits.

Accepted references and private values

Use @ in the composer, select Parameter Store, then select a key to insert a short reference such as @ronan_server. You can also type @rona to search directly, or paste the complete reference. The menu shows field names. Aliases, descriptions, and tags help with search; submitted references resolve the canonical key exactly.

Settings → Parameters → Parameter binding engine is off by default. With it on, an accepted reference gives the Agent exact JSON source pointers and types in fields, full Context JSON, description, aliases and tags. Tools receive exact saved values without requiring the Agent to retype them. This works with arbitrary nested JSON; no SSH-specific format is required. The Agent can explicitly read content when needed for reasoning, subject to existing redaction settings.

Pointers address the saved Value JSON itself. For {"repo_path":"~/work/repo"}, the source pointer is /repo_path; the reference name is not a filesystem path. A destination pointer addresses the selected tool's arguments, such as /cwd. The Agent chooses the mapping using the task and tool schema; the runtime does not infer field meanings or repair guessed paths. Empty source pointers select the whole saved value. Object keys use JSON Pointer escaping (~ becomes ~0, / becomes ~1), and arrays use numeric indexes.

The initial description includes nested pointers within the existing aggregate parameter prompt limit. When fields are omitted, fields_complete: false and an exact next_action retrieve the next entries. read_parameter(key=..., pointer=..., view="fields", offset=0, limit=16) lists pointers and types without scalar values; its pointers remain absolute even when browsing a subtree. Offsets count entries, and limits must be integers from 1 through 64. Follow the supplied next-page action. view="value" and view="structure" retain their existing responses and do not accept paging arguments. Explicit field pages are not cut by tool-result head/tail previews; a capacity rejection supplies a smaller-page call, or reports that even one entry cannot fit.

Invalid source pointers produce bounded valid-pointer suggestions and a field-list action for the deepest valid ancestor. No suggested field is selected or executed automatically. A field marked unaddressable_descendants has descendants beyond the existing pointer-length limit; bind that ancestor or use automatic code inputs to access its contents. Both the full saved parameter expansion and the model-facing description still obey the existing size limit; paging does not bypass admission limits.

Turning the toggle off restores the previous behavior: ordinary Value JSON is included directly in the Parameters prompt section, using existing redaction settings. The change needs no restart and applies to newly accepted tasks. Queued tasks, retries and Continue retain the mode and values captured when accepted. Each new scheduled occurrence uses the current setting.

Shell and Python receive saved values through inputs["parameters"][key]; Shell also receives JSON in OF_INPUT_PARAMETERS. Other compatible tools use explicit field bindings. Invalid field paths, conflicting literal values and incompatible types stop the call before execution. The engine does not guess fields or interpolate command strings. Put values in Value JSON and explanatory guidance in Context JSON. The separate learned-workflow editor can save reviewed corrected calls and fresh links between earlier outputs and later inputs. Existing saved-request workflows retain their behavior.

Review a successful binding for future tasks

For a task accepted with parameter binding enabled, open Parameter bindings in its run footer, beside Artifacts. Eligible successful calls show Review binding. The recorded source fields and destinations must be available; automatic parameter injection, matching values or an Agent's statement alone do not qualify a call.

Open the review, check its masked original call and selected sources, then choose Preview binding. You can change the source/destination choices or name the mapping. Changed bindings are labeled not executed: the original successful execution remains separate evidence. Values come from that call's accepted snapshot; this review does not refresh it from current saved parameters.

Choose Approve and save for future tasks after reviewing the workspace, Gateway and matching constraints. Approval saves reusable intent without pausing, resuming or retrying the current task. Closing the panel also leaves the task running normally. The rule becomes available to newly accepted tasks that match its constraints. Already accepted or queued tasks, restart and Continue keep their original approval boundary; each later scheduled occurrence captures its own boundary when created.

Manage saved mappings opens the Parameter Store library. Execution success, approval and Confirm correct result are separate assessments. A stale preview or changed saved revision requires another review; duplicate approval does not create another equivalent reusable rule. The binding-review flow diagrams explain evidence reconstruction, atomic saving and later call admission.

Correct a tool call and remember its mapping

When parameter binding is enabled for the accepted task, its desktop or mobile task card shows Stop and map parameters, including in immersive mode, when Show status is off, or when activity is collapsed. Before the first eligible tool call, the shortcut is disabled and explains when it becomes available. Clicking requests Pause immediately and opens a call picker with failures first. Choose the call whose arguments need correction; successful calls and individual parallel/sequence children can also be selected.

Use the persistent Help button or open How to map parameters in the picker or editor for a quick reference, including the SSH field example, preview and Apply steps, remembered reuse, and what Close and Cancel do. The guide stays available while you choose and edit a call.

Failed tool calls also offer Stop and map parameters. The tool inspector offers it for successful calls whose result was wrong. Displaying or ignoring the action does not interrupt execution. Clicking it requests the normal cooperative Pause; accepted work settles before Apply becomes available. Desktop and mobile use the same editor.

Choose a source beside each destination. The searchable field tree includes accepted parameters and earlier complete results from this task. Accept current saved values explicitly adds or refreshes a source; otherwise the task's accepted values stay pinned. The reveal action uses the existing audited Parameter Store route and labels the current saved value separately from accepted task values.

Review the masked preview, then choose Apply mapping and let Agent retry. The mapping is saved before a structured correction is added to the task. Apply itself executes no tool; the Agent chooses its next call. If the task ended, a matching later retry succeeded, or the selected call has an uncertain outcome, save for future use instead. Reconcile an uncertain operation before any retry. Remember for this workspace and Gateway is selected initially; clear it for one-time correction of a live task. Future-only saving requires Remember to stay enabled.

Closing the panel leaves the session recoverable. It does not cancel an in-flight request or resume a paused task. Cancel correction waits for accepted work to settle and resumes only a matching pause initiated by this correction; another pause stays in place. Continue parameter mapping reopens the session after closing or reloading. If Apply was interrupted, Finish applying correction resumes the saved intent and accepted values. An applying correction must finish recovery before it can be treated as complete. Changed revisions or previews require reopening/reviewing; repeated application of the same saved intent does not add another amendment. The correction flow diagrams show pause ownership, frozen inputs and the recoverable write stages.

Literal ssh and sshpass … ssh calls expose username, host, port and authentication separately. Password mappings use sshpass -e with a private environment value. Passwords do not enter learned templates, correction text or previews. Remote commands and unrelated SSH options are preserved. Compound local scripts, local expansions and ambiguous syntax require simplification or structured inputs; they are never rewritten heuristically.

The Parameter Store page includes Remembered parameter mappings, with revision history, enable/disable controls and outcome feedback. An exit code of zero records execution success. Confirm correct result separately records your assessment. Incorrect mapping suspends that revision until reviewed; network failures alone do not suspend it.

Teach an ordered workflow

From the tool inspector, choose Teach workflow from this run. Select completed calls in the intended order, review the dependency list, and save the sequence. Map dependent inputs first when a step needs an earlier output. Each selected step depends on the preceding step; output bindings name their exact producer. This initial version supports one workspace and Gateway per sequence, without inferred branches or loops. Select one to 64 distinct successful calls. A result-producing call must precede the step that consumes it; missing mapping history or a suspended mapping requires review before saving.

Open Learned workflows in the mapping library and explicitly choose Run learned workflow. The Agent issues each step. Existing workflow guards enforce the reviewed arguments, dependencies and current-run receipt ownership. New tasks accept current parameter values; a previous task's result is never substituted as fresh output. Parameter binding must be enabled to launch a learned workflow. The current enabled revision runs in its original workspace and Gateway. Launch creates a dedicated conversation and an ordinary queued task; retrying the same launch request recovers that task. The teaching and launch diagrams explain this boundary. This is separate from saved-request workflows.

Ordinary typed and untyped references capture literal accepted values in the run checkpoint. Auth-protected profiles capture permitted identity/revision projections instead; their provider adapters retain responsibility for private authority. PARAMETERS optionally masks the model-facing copy, independently of MODEL_INPUT. Sensitive-record metadata controls only that record's projection and never promotes ordinary values such as https or local into global replacement material. Reference resolution adds no model call. Private credential fields retain their existing handling.

Manual tasks capture parameters when accepted, including time spent in the queue. Editing or deleting a parameter does not change an accepted task. New tasks use current values. Scheduled tasks keep symbolic references and capture current values for each occurrence, including one-time future tasks. For ordinary JSON values, resuming or continuing a task reuses its persisted contents, including after restart. Tasks captured using the former reference format must be submitted again; their old bindings are never silently reinterpreted.

Ordinary snapshots survive restart, edit and deletion using their accepted values. Older version-2 tasks retain inline prompt behavior. Private authentication profiles continue to use their existing credential rules; missing historical values are not fabricated. Parameter storage remains plaintext. See Redaction for optional visibility controls and Parameter storage, acceptance and exact inputs for storage ownership, revision checks and binding failure boundaries.

Resource and action names are reserved after key normalization: gateway, context, file, artifact, runafter, run_after, special, special_actions, parameter, parameters, use_memory, agent, ask, and plan. Case, whitespace and hyphen variants normalize to the same identities. Existing conflicting entries remain manageable; rename them before selecting them with @. Keys containing spaces use their normalized form in references, such as @my_server. Dots and colons inside a key are literal parts of its name; @key.field does not select a field. Emails, escaped references, inline code, and fenced code remain literal text. References follow the composer's existing whitespace boundary rule.

Unknown canonical names leave the task at Needs input until corrected or explicitly accepted with Use as literal text. Invalid reference tokens remain literal: npm install @scope/package is not a valid parameter reference. A pasted curl --data @payload.json requires a literal choice when no payload.json parameter exists; put pasted commands in backticks to prevent reference parsing. Mixed prompts capture existing canonical keys while holding the task for unresolved names. The runtime never guesses a similar key for a misspelled or deleted name.

If the prompt contains no parameter candidates, or every candidate is explicitly literal, no Parameters section is added and no parameter usage is recorded. The empty accepted snapshot is preserved across retries, queue dispatch, restart, resume, and Continue, even if a matching parameter is created later. New tasks and each scheduled occurrence use the names currently in the store. A pasted name that already matches a saved key still resolves; wrap commands in inline backticks or a fenced code block to force literal treatment.

Disabled or unavailable storage, invalid stored JSON, and bindings larger than the configured parameter context limit still stop the task before inference. Restore the store or correct the referenced objects; the runtime never truncates JSON.

For a task held at Needs input, enable Show runtime issues in the chat to see the specific failure and recovery steps. Runtime messages distinguish missing canonical keys, disabled resolution, an unavailable store, failed reads, invalid records or saved bindings, invalid JSON, and expansion limits. Storage errors include a specific cause such as a busy database, denied access, full disk, database corruption, or an I/O failure when the storage driver reports that cause.

Size errors show the combined character count, configured limit, excess, and up to five largest entries, including their metadata. The default is 4,000 characters for the entire expanded Parameters section, including its header. The startup setting agent_parameter_prompt_max_chars (environment variable AOR_AGENT_PARAMETER_PROMPT_MAX_CHARS) changes this limit after a server restart. An entry appearing in the @ palette does not guarantee that its full contents fit.

Diagnostics contain parameter keys and counts, never stored values or raw storage exception messages. After correcting the cause, choose Check again. The held task retains the same Runtime message as it updates or resolves; the visibility toggle does not resume execution. Existing held tasks show known historical causes on reload; Check again captures fuller diagnostics when older records lack them.

An accepted task can remain held without starting a model or tool. Correcting its references preserves the task and checks the displayed issue revision; if another client has already changed it, refresh before responding. Once resolved, it returns to the normal queue and still waits for its dependencies and available capacity. Cancelling the held task prevents that intent from starting.

A parameter usage/audit failure is separate from a missing reference. It can be reported after the task has already been accepted. Check the saved task before submitting another copy; a successful retry updates the same Runtime issue. The task admission architecture explains the storage and retry boundaries.

Gmail OAuth App stores the existing Google application's configuration. gmail.connect creates the Gmail Account parameter after consent. Account projection includes email, linked app and authorization state, omitting OAuth secrets. Automatic refresh updates the same account record. Unlike a fixed connection snapshot, Gmail resolves the current account authorization on every provider call; rename/deletion takes effect immediately. Multiple Gmail accounts are normal separate parameters. See Gmail Integration.

Transient Database authentication

database.discover_schema and database.execute use the selected profile's configured host, port, and dbname. Optional auth_values accepts only literal user and password strings for that invocation. Historical profile aliases remain readable, but tool arguments use the canonical user spelling.

Missing authentication returns credential_required with missing_fields and executed=false. The Agent uses ordinary ask_user to request all missing values in one reply, then retries with auth_values on its next normal decision. These values do not update Parameter Store, schema metadata, or Working Context. To save a value, explicitly edit the parameter. Missing host/port/dbname instead returns database_profile_incomplete; correct the profile or select another configured profile. A transient password cannot change the database target. SQL validation and mutation approval still apply. Database redaction affects projections only; the Gateway receives the same literal execution environment with redaction on/off.

Auth and Email profiles

Version-one oauth2_client and oauth2_connection profiles configure shared OAuth/OIDC authorization; email_smtp fixes an outbound sender and SMTP transport. Their templates are detached prefills. Private fields in these profiles are excluded from model bindings, audits and shell environments independently of optional redaction. Read Authentication and outbound Email for setup, callback URLs, provider defaults, attachment limits and uncertain-delivery handling.

Shared Google Workspace profiles

google_oauth_app contains the registered desktop/web client and selected feature IDs; google_account contains provider-verified subject/email, granted scopes, derived features and private tokens. Both use version 1, strict unknown-field rejection and unconditional safe projections. auth.google_connect creates or updates the account through Parameter Store only. OAuth refresh uses transactional compare/update checks against account and app revisions; neither discovery nor template selection migrates existing Gmail profiles. See Shared Google Workspace identity for setup and scope policy.

Microsoft 365 profiles

The Microsoft 365 integration adds microsoft_oauth_app and microsoft365_account. Public PKCE requires no client secret. Account access/refresh tokens and confidential-client secrets remain private even when ordinary redaction is disabled. Use the same account key for reconnect or incremental consent.

Slack profiles

The Slack integration adds slack_oauth_app and slack_workspace. The app stores a private client secret and explicit bot/user scope selections. Each workspace profile pins one verified team and principal; access and rotation tokens remain private. Configure a registered HTTPS callback, then use slack.connect. Disconnect clears local credentials without uninstalling the app.

The GitHub integration adds github_account for exact github.com user PAT authority, separate from the existing git_repository transport profile. Its token is always private. The profile records login/account ID, an explicit repository allowlist, declared permissions and a deliberate fine-grained or classic credential type. Store timestamps own creation/update history. Accepted references cannot expand capability policy.
